                                        <div class="paragraph-component-text field_component_sec_blocks-item odd">  <div class="text--block-content section-block-content">
    <div class="comp-txt">
                            <div class="field paragraph field_component_text_content  odd-t text_long"><h2>What is UNICEF?</h2><p dir="ltr">UNICEF is the United Nations Children’s Fund, working in the world’s toughest places to reach the most disadvantaged children and adolescents – and to protect the rights of every child, everywhere.</p><p dir="ltr">One of the world’s largest providers of vaccines, UNICEF supports child health and nutrition, safe water and sanitation, quality education and skill building, HIV prevention and treatment for mothers and babies, and the protection of children and adolescents from violence and exploitation. </p><p dir="ltr">Before, during and after humanitarian emergencies, UNICEF is on the ground, bringing life-saving help and hope to children and families.</p><p><a href="/what-we-do">Learn more</a> about what we do to help children survive, thrive, and fulfil their potential.</p></div>
            </div>
      </div>
</div>
                                        <div class="paragraph-component-anchor field_component_sec_blocks-item even">    <div class="paragraph paragraph--type--component-anchor paragraph--view-mode--default">
                    <a class="anchor-space" id="2"></a>

            </div>
  </div>
                                        <div class="paragraph-component-text field_component_sec_blocks-item odd">  <div class="text--block-content section-block-content">
    <div class="comp-txt">
                            <div class="field paragraph field_component_text_content  odd-t text_long"><h2>Where does UNICEF work? </h2><p dir="ltr">UNICEF works in <a href="/where-we-work">more than 190 countries and territories</a> and in the world’s toughest places to reach the children and young people in greatest need.  </p><p>We operate through country offices around the world, as well as <a href="https://www.unicef.org/unicef-national-committees">32 National Committees</a>, seven regional offices, a <a href="https://www.unicef-irc.org/">research centre</a> in Florence, a <a href="https://www.unicef.org/supply/">supply operation</a> in Copenhagen, a <a href="/gssc/work-with-gssc">shared services centre</a> in Budapest, as well as other offices in <a href="https://www.unicef.org/eu/">Brussels</a>, Geneva, Seoul, and <a href="https://www.unicef.org/tokyo/">Tokyo</a>. Some 85 per cent of our staff are located in the field. UNICEF headquarters are in New York.</p></div>
            </div>
      </div>
</div>
                                        <div class="paragraph-component-anchor field_component_sec_blocks-item even">    <div class="paragraph paragraph--type--component-anchor paragraph--view-mode--default">
                    <a class="anchor-space" id="3"></a>

            </div>
  </div>
                                        <div class="paragraph-component-text field_component_sec_blocks-item odd">  <div class="text--block-content section-block-content">
    <div class="comp-txt">
                            <div class="field paragraph field_component_text_content  odd-t text_long"><h2>What does the acronym UNICEF stand for?</h2><p dir="ltr">On 11 December 1946, the United Nations established UNICEF to meet the emergency needs of children in post-war Europe and China. Our full name was the United Nations International Children's Emergency Fund. </p><p>In 1950, the UNICEF mandate was broadened to address the long-term needs of children and women in developing countries everywhere. UNICEF became a permanent part of the United Nations system in 1953, when our name was shortened to the United Nations Children's Fund. However, UNICEF retained its original acronym. </p></div>
            </div>
      </div>
</div>
                                        <div class="paragraph-component-anchor field_component_sec_blocks-item even">    <div class="paragraph paragraph--type--component-anchor paragraph--view-mode--default">
                    <a class="anchor-space" id="4"></a>

            </div>
  </div>
                                        <div class="paragraph-component-text field_component_sec_blocks-item odd">  <div class="text--block-content section-block-content">
    <div class="comp-txt">
                            <div class="field paragraph field_component_text_content  odd-t text_long"><h2>How can I make a donation to UNICEF?</h2><p dir="ltr">Thanks for your interest in supporting UNICEF. Our work depends entirely on voluntary contributions. <a href="https://donate.unicef.org/donate/now">Donate now</a> or explore other ways to <a href="/take-action">take action</a>. </p></div>
            </div>
      </div>
</div>
                                        <div class="paragraph-component-anchor field_component_sec_blocks-item even">    <div class="paragraph paragraph--type--component-anchor paragraph--view-mode--default">
                    <a class="anchor-space" id="5"></a>

            </div>
  </div>
                                        <div class="paragraph-component-text field_component_sec_blocks-item odd">  <div class="text--block-content section-block-content">
    <div class="comp-txt">
                            <div class="field paragraph field_component_text_content  odd-t text_long"><h2>Where can I get the latest data on issues affecting children?</h2><p dir="ltr">UNICEF collects data to monitor the situation of children and young people around the world. Find data by country and topic, data visualizations and dashboards, and more <a href="https://data.unicef.org/">on data.unicef.org</a>.</p></div>
            </div>
      </div>
</div>
                                        <div class="paragraph-component-anchor field_component_sec_blocks-item even">    <div class="paragraph paragraph--type--component-anchor paragraph--view-mode--default">
                    <a class="anchor-space" id="6"></a>

            </div>
  </div>
                                        <div class="paragraph-component-text field_component_sec_blocks-item odd">  <div class="text--block-content section-block-content">
    <div class="comp-txt">
                            <div class="field paragraph field_component_text_content  odd-t text_long"><h2>Where can I find UNICEF publications?</h2><p dir="ltr">For UNICEF publications and other resources, including the latest State of the World’s Children report and Annual Report, visit our <a href="https://www.unicef.org/research-and-reports">publications section</a>.</p><p dir="ltr"><a href="https://www.unicef.org/innocenti/">Innocenti – Global Office of Research and Foresight</a> drives change for children and young people by generating evidence, collecting data, featuring the voices of children and offering foresight on frontier issues and emerging practices.</p></div>
            </div>
      </div>
</div>
                                        <div class="paragraph-component-anchor field_component_sec_blocks-item even">    <div class="paragraph paragraph--type--component-anchor paragraph--view-mode--default">
                    <a class="anchor-space" id="7"></a>

            </div>
  </div>
                                        <div class="paragraph-component-text field_component_sec_blocks-item odd">  <div class="text--block-content section-block-content">
    <div class="comp-txt">
                            <div class="field paragraph field_component_text_content  odd-t text_long"><h2>Where does UNICEF get its funding?</h2><p dir="ltr">UNICEF’s work is funded entirely through the voluntary support of millions of people around the world and our partners in government, civil society and the private sector. For detailed information, go to the latest <a href="/reports/unicef-annual-report" data-entity-type="node" data-entity-uuid="340efa5d-9279-4a19-8a7e-89cc58128685" data-entity-substitution="canonical" title="UNICEF Annual Report">Annual Report</a> or visit our <a href="/partnerships/funding">funding</a> pages.</p></div>
            </div>
      </div>
</div>
                                        <div class="paragraph-component-anchor field_component_sec_blocks-item even">    <div class="paragraph paragraph--type--component-anchor paragraph--view-mode--default">
                    <a class="anchor-space" id="8"></a>

            </div>
  </div>
                                        <div class="paragraph-component-text field_component_sec_blocks-item odd">  <div class="text--block-content section-block-content">
    <div class="comp-txt">
                            <div class="field paragraph field_component_text_content  odd-t text_long"><h2>How is UNICEF accountable for its work?</h2><p dir="ltr">UNICEF has an established <a href="/legal#information-disclosure-policy">Information Disclosure Policy </a>that outlines explicitly its commitment to making information about programmes and operations available to the public. As a signatory to the<a href="https://iatistandard.org/en/"> International Aid Transparency Initiative</a> (IATI), UNICEF provides open and comprehensive public access to operational and programme data through its <a href="https://open.unicef.org/">Transparency Portal.</a> </p></div>
            </div>
      </div>
</div>
                                        <div class="paragraph-component-anchor field_component_sec_blocks-item even">    <div class="paragraph paragraph--type--component-anchor paragraph--view-mode--default">
                    <a class="anchor-space" id="9"></a>

            </div>
  </div>
                                        <div class="paragraph-component-text field_component_sec_blocks-item odd">  <div class="text--block-content section-block-content">
    <div class="comp-txt">
                            <div class="field paragraph field_component_text_content  odd-t text_long"><h2>What is the UNICEF Executive Board?</h2><p>The Executive Board is the governing body of UNICEF, providing intergovernmental support and oversight to the organization, in accordance with the overall policy guidance of the United Nations General Assembly and the Economic and Social Council. <a href="https://www.unicef.org/executiveboard/">Learn more</a> about Executive Board members, sessions, decisions and more.</p></div>
            </div>
      </div>
</div>
                                        <div class="paragraph-component-anchor field_component_sec_blocks-item even">    <div class="paragraph paragraph--type--component-anchor paragraph--view-mode--default">
                    <a class="anchor-space" id="10"></a>

            </div>
  </div>
                                        <div class="paragraph-component-text field_component_sec_blocks-item odd">  <div class="text--block-content section-block-content">
    <div class="comp-txt">
                            <div class="field paragraph field_component_text_content  odd-t text_long"><h2>How can I apply for a job with UNICEF?</h2><p dir="ltr">Thanks for your interest in joining our team. We’re looking for committed professionals willing to engage in the challenging work of advocating for children's rights, helping to meet their basic needs and expanding their opportunities to reach their full potential. Check out <a href="https://jobs.unicef.org/en-us/listing/">current opportunities</a>. </p></div>
            </div>
      </div>
</div>
                                        <div class="paragraph-component-anchor field_component_sec_blocks-item even">    <div class="paragraph paragraph--type--component-anchor paragraph--view-mode--default">
                    <a class="anchor-space" id="11"></a>

            </div>
  </div>
                                        <div class="paragraph-component-text field_component_sec_blocks-item odd">  <div class="text--block-content section-block-content">
    <div class="comp-txt">
                            <div class="field paragraph field_component_text_content  odd-t text_long"><h2>What is the Junior Professional Officers Programme?</h2><p dir="ltr">The Junior Professional Officers (JPO) programme provides young professionals interested in pursuing a career in development an opportunity to acquire hands-on experience in multilateral cooperation. JPOs work in one of UNICEF's programme areas, either at headquarters or in a country or regional office. <a href="https://www.unicef.org/careers/junior-professional-officer-programme">Learn more about the JPO programme</a>. </p></div>
            </div>
      </div>
</div>
                                        <div class="paragraph-component-anchor field_component_sec_blocks-item even">    <div class="paragraph paragraph--type--component-anchor paragraph--view-mode--default">
                    <a class="anchor-space" id="12"></a>

            </div>
  </div>
                                        <div class="paragraph-component-text field_component_sec_blocks-item odd">  <div class="text--block-content section-block-content">
    <div class="comp-txt">
                            <div class="field paragraph field_component_text_content  odd-t text_long"><h2>How can I find an internship at UNICEF?</h2><p dir="ltr">Our Internship Programme offers students the opportunity to acquire practical experience in UNICEF's work. <a href="https://www.unicef.org/careers/internships">Learn more about eligibility requirements and how to apply</a>.</p></div>
            </div>
      </div>
</div>
                                        <div class="paragraph-component-anchor field_component_sec_blocks-item even">    <div class="paragraph paragraph--type--component-anchor paragraph--view-mode--default">
                    <a class="anchor-space" id="13"></a>

            </div>
  </div>
                                        <div class="paragraph-component-text field_component_sec_blocks-item odd">  <div class="text--block-content section-block-content">
    <div class="comp-txt">
                            <div class="field paragraph field_component_text_content  odd-t text_long"><h2>How can I volunteer to work for UNICEF?</h2><p dir="ltr">If you have an undergraduate degree, several years of work experience and are interested in long-term volunteer opportunities, you may be eligible for entry into the <a href="https://www.unv.org/">United Nations Volunteer</a> (UNV) programme. This is a United Nations common programme that recruits volunteers for assignments throughout the United Nations system, including UNICEF. </p><p dir="ltr">For additional information on volunteer opportunities, visit our <a href="https://www.unicef.org/careers/volunteers-unicef">volunteers page</a>.</p></div>
            </div>
      </div>
</div>
                                        <div class="paragraph-component-anchor field_component_sec_blocks-item even">    <div class="paragraph paragraph--type--component-anchor paragraph--view-mode--default">
                    <a class="anchor-space" id="14"></a>

            </div>
  </div>
                                        <div class="paragraph-component-text field_component_sec_blocks-item odd">  <div class="text--block-content section-block-content">
    <div class="comp-txt">
                            <div class="field paragraph field_component_text_content  odd-t text_long"><h2>How can I partner with UNICEF?</h2><p>UNICEF works in some of the hardest-to-reach places to protect children’s rights and safeguard their futures. But we can’t do it alone. We unite with the public sector, private sector and civil society in over 190 countries and territories. Whether you’re an organization or an individual supporter, <a href="/partnerships" target="_blank">learn more about opportunities for partnering with UNICEF</a>.</p></div>
            </div>
      </div>
</div>
                                        <div class="paragraph-component-anchor field_component_sec_blocks-item even">    <div class="paragraph paragraph--type--component-anchor paragraph--view-mode--default">
                    <a class="anchor-space" id="15"></a>

            </div>
  </div>
                                        <div class="paragraph-component-text field_component_sec_blocks-item odd">  <div class="text--block-content section-block-content">
    <div class="comp-txt">
                            <div class="field paragraph field_component_text_content  odd-t text_long"><h2>I am a young person. What do you have for me?</h2><p dir="ltr">If you are between 13 and 24 years old, check out how people like you are getting involved and join <a href="https://www.u-report.org/" target="_blank">U-Report</a> a global online community for young people who want to make a difference in the world.</p></div>
            </div>
      </div>
</div>
                                        <div class="paragraph-component-anchor field_component_sec_blocks-item even">    <div class="paragraph paragraph--type--component-anchor paragraph--view-mode--default">
                    <a class="anchor-space" id="16"></a>

            </div>
  </div>
                                        <div class="paragraph-component-text field_component_sec_blocks-item odd">  <div class="text--block-content section-block-content">
    <div class="comp-txt">
                            <div class="field paragraph field_component_text_content  odd-t text_long"><h2>I am a member of the press. Where do I go for information?</h2><p dir="ltr">Our <a href="/media/press-centre">Press Centre</a> has the latest press releases, official statements, expert sources, and more. For additional information, you can also <a href="/media/contact-us">contact our Media team</a>. </p></div>
            </div>
      </div>
</div>
                                        <div class="paragraph-component-anchor field_component_sec_blocks-item even">    <div class="paragraph paragraph--type--component-anchor paragraph--view-mode--default">
                    <a class="anchor-space" id="17"></a>

            </div>
  </div>
                                        <div class="paragraph-component-text field_component_sec_blocks-item odd">  <div class="text--block-content section-block-content">
    <div class="comp-txt">
                            <div class="field paragraph field_component_text_content  odd-t text_long"><h2>How can I obtain UNICEF videos, photos and other multimedia materials? </h2><p dir="ltr">UNICEF photographs, videos, audio, print materials and other assets are available to professional media and others for authorized use. Visit our <a href="https://weshare.unicef.org/C.aspx?VP3=CMS3&VF=Home">WeShare</a> database to explore our multimedia packages. </p></div>
            </div>
      </div>
</div>
                                        <div class="paragraph-component-anchor field_component_sec_blocks-item even">    <div class="paragraph paragraph--type--component-anchor paragraph--view-mode--default">
                    <a class="anchor-space" id="18"></a>

            </div>
  </div>
                                        <div class="paragraph-component-text field_component_sec_blocks-item odd">  <div class="text--block-content section-block-content">
    <div class="comp-txt">
                            <div class="field paragraph field_component_text_content  odd-t text_long"><h2>What are the terms of use for the reproduction of materials found on the website, including photographs and graphic designs?</h2><p dir="ltr">If you wish to mirror, reproduce, republish or translate any of the information available on the website for wider dissemination, please refer to UNICEF’s <a href="/legal#copyright">copyright and terms of use.</a></p><p dir="ltr">The unauthorized use of the UNICEF name and logo is against international law and is expressly forbidden.</p></div>
            </div>
      </div>
</div>
                                        <div class="paragraph-component-anchor field_component_sec_blocks-item even">    <div class="paragraph paragraph--type--component-anchor paragraph--view-mode--default">
                    <a class="anchor-space" id="19"></a>

            </div>
  </div>
                                        <div class="paragraph-component-text field_component_sec_blocks-item odd">  <div class="text--block-content section-block-content">
    <div class="comp-txt">
                            <div class="field paragraph field_component_text_content  odd-t text_long"><h2>I wish to report fraud, abuse or wrongdoing. Whom can I contact?</h2><p dir="ltr">UNICEF takes all reports of alleged wrongdoing and misconduct seriously. For information on how and what to report, visit our <a href="/report-wrongdoing">How to Report Wrongdoing</a> guide.</p><p dir="ltr">If you have information on fraud, corruption, sexual harassment, abuse of authority, sexual exploitation and abuse, or waste and mismanagement involving UNICEF staff, consultants, institutional contractors, vendors or implementing partners, please report the matter directly to UNICEF's <a href="https://www.unicef.org/auditandinvestigation/">Office of Internal Audit and Investigations</a>. </p></div>
            </div>
      </div>
</div>
                                        <div class="paragraph-component-anchor field_component_sec_blocks-item even">    <div class="paragraph paragraph--type--component-anchor paragraph--view-mode--default">
                    <a class="anchor-space" id="20"></a>

            </div>
  </div>
                                        <div class="paragraph-component-text field_component_sec_blocks-item odd">  <div class="text--block-content section-block-content">
    <div class="comp-txt">
                            <div class="field paragraph field_component_text_content  odd-t text_long"><h2>I am having difficulty finding specific information on UNICEF.org. Where should I go?</h2><p dir="ltr">We’re sorry for any inconvenience, but we’re building a new UNICEF.org. During the transition some pages will be swapped out for new ones. Please try using our search and if you still can’t find what you’re looking for, please come back later. We are updating pages and sections daily.</p></div>
            </div>
      </div>
</div>

Whom can I contact?   I am having difficulty finding specific information on UNICEF.org . Where should I go? What is UNICEF? UNICEF is the United Nations Children’s Fund, working in the world’s toughest places to reach the most disadvantaged children and adolescents – and to protect the rights of every child, everywhere. One of the world’s largest providers of vaccines, UNICEF supports child health and nutrition, safe water and sanitation, quality education and skill building, HIV prevention and treatment for mothers and babies, and the protection of children and adolescents from violence and exploitation.  Before, during and after humanitarian emergencies, UNICEF is on the ground, bringing life-saving help and hope to children and families. Learn more about what we do to help children survive, thrive, and fulfil their potential. Where does UNICEF work?  UNICEF works in more than 190 countries and territories and in the world’s toughest places to reach the children and young people in greatest need.   We operate through country offices around the world, as well as 32 National Committees , seven regional offices, a research centre in Florence, a supply operation in Copenhagen, a shared services centre in Budapest, as well as other offices in Brussels , Geneva, Seoul, and Tokyo . Some 85 per cent of our staff are located in the field. UNICEF headquarters are in New York. What does the acronym UNICEF stand for? On 11 December 1946, the United Nations established UNICEF to meet the emergency needs of children in post-war Europe and China. Our full name was the United Nations International Children's Emergency Fund.  In 1950, the UNICEF mandate was broadened to address the long-term needs of children and women in developing countries everywhere. UNICEF became a permanent part of the United Nations system in 1953, when our name was shortened to the United Nations Children's Fund. However, UNICEF retained its original acronym.  How can I make a donation to UNICEF? Thanks for your interest in supporting UNICEF. Our work depends entirely on voluntary contributions. Donate now or explore other ways to take action .  Where can I get the latest data on issues affecting children? UNICEF collects data to monitor the situation of children and young people around the world. Find data by country and topic, data visualizations and dashboards, and more on data.unicef.org . Where can I find UNICEF publications? For UNICEF publications and other resources, including the latest State of the World’s Children report and Annual Report, visit our publications section . Innocenti – Global Office of Research and Foresight drives change for children and young people by generating evidence, collecting data, featuring the voices of children and offering foresight on frontier issues and emerging practices. Where does UNICEF get its funding? UNICEF’s work is funded entirely through the voluntary support of millions of people around the world and our partners in government, civil society and the private sector. For detailed information, go to the latest Annual Report  or visit our funding pages. How is UNICEF accountable for its work? UNICEF has an established Information Disclosure Policy that outlines explicitly its commitment to making information about programmes and operations available to the public. As a signatory to the International Aid Transparency Initiative (IATI), UNICEF provides open and comprehensive public access to operational and programme data through its Transparency Portal.   What is the UNICEF Executive Board? The Executive Board is the governing body of UNICEF, providing intergovernmental support and oversight to the organization, in accordance with the overall policy guidance of the United Nations General Assembly and the Economic and Social Council. Learn more  about Executive Board members, sessions, decisions and more. How can I apply for a job with UNICEF? Thanks for your interest in joining our team. We’re looking for committed professionals willing to engage in the challenging work of advocating for children's rights, helping to meet their basic needs and expanding their opportunities to reach their full potential. Check out current opportunities .  What is the Junior Professional Officers Programme? The Junior Professional Officers (JPO) programme provides young professionals interested in pursuing a career in development an opportunity to acquire hands-on experience in multilateral cooperation. JPOs work in one of UNICEF's programme areas, either at headquarters or in a country or regional office. Learn more about the JPO programme .  How can I find an internship at UNICEF? Our Internship Programme offers students the opportunity to acquire practical experience in UNICEF's work. Learn more about eligibility requirements and how to apply . How can I volunteer to work for UNICEF? If you have an undergraduate degree, several years of work experience and are interested in long-term volunteer opportunities, you may be eligible for entry into the United Nations Volunteer (UNV) programme. This is a United Nations common programme that recruits volunteers for assignments throughout the United Nations system, including UNICEF.  For additional information on volunteer opportunities, visit our volunteers page . How can I partner with UNICEF? UNICEF works in some of the hardest-to-reach places to protect children’s rights and safeguard their futures. But we can’t do it alone. We unite with the public sector, private sector and civil society in over 190 countries and territories. Whether you’re an organization or an individual supporter,  learn more about opportunities for partnering with UNICEF . I am a young person. What do you have for me? If you are between 13 and 24 years old, check out how people like you are getting involved and join U-Report a global online community for young people who want to make a difference in the world. I am a member of the press. Where do I go for information? Our Press Centre has the latest press releases, official statements, expert sources, and more. For additional information, you can also contact our Media team .  How can I obtain UNICEF videos, photos and other multimedia materials?  UNICEF photographs, videos, audio, print materials and other assets are available to professional media and others for authorized use. Visit our WeShare database to explore our multimedia packages.  What are the terms of use for the reproduction of materials found on the website, including photographs and graphic designs? If you wish to mirror, reproduce, republish or translate any of the information available on the website for wider dissemination, please refer to UNICEF’s copyright and terms of use. The unauthorized use of the UNICEF name and logo is against international law and is expressly forbidden. I wish to report fraud, abuse or wrongdoing. Whom can I contact? UNICEF takes all reports of alleged wrongdoing and misconduct seriously. For information on how and what to report, visit our How to Report Wrongdoing guide. If you have information on fraud, corruption, sexual harassment, abuse of authority, sexual exploitation and abuse, or waste and mismanagement involving UNICEF staff, consultants, institutional contractors, vendors or implementing partners, please report the matter directly to UNICEF's  Office of Internal Audit and Investigations .  I am having difficulty finding specific information on UNICEF.org. Where should I go? We’re sorry for any inconvenience, but we’re building a new UNICEF.org. During the transition some pages will be swapped out for new ones. Please try using our search and if you still can’t find what you’re looking for, please come back later. We are updating pages and sections daily. This work is in line with UNICEF’s globally recognized mandate and its support of national priorities.

                            <div class="field paragraph field_component_text_content  odd-t text_long"><p>UNICEF works in over 190 countries and territories to save children’s lives, to defend their rights, and to help them fulfil their potential, from early childhood through adolescence. Our organization’s activities focus on: </p><ul><li>providing a safe and inclusive environment for children through adequate protection,</li><li>reducing child mortality and child poverty by working to reach the most vulnerable children,</li><li>supporting quality learning for every girl and boy, especially those left behind,</li><li>reaching children and families with lifesaving aid and long-term assistance in emergencies,</li><li>empower girls and women so that they can play a full role in society. </li></ul></div>

                            <div class="field paragraph field_component_text_content  odd-t text_long"><p>UNICEF staff in the field are doing all they can to reach the most vulnerable children across the world.     <div class="comp-txt">
                            <div class="field paragraph field_component_text_content  odd-t text_long"><h3 class="text-align-center">What we do </h3><p>We have over 400 dedicated staff members from all over the globe who provide services to UNICEF’s offices and staff worldwide, benchmarked against the highest industry standards. </p><ul><li>Human resources – we help new colleagues onboard, parting colleagues offboard, and we take care of the HR needs of all staff members in-between</li><li>Payroll – we coordinate salary disbursement globally</li><li>Finance – we process invoices and provide a range of financial services to keep UNICEF programmes for children running</li><li>Global helpdesk – we support staff in taking care of their work-related administrative tasks </li></ul><p>Thanks to the GSSC, the reduced time - over 27,000 hours saved - that UNICEF offices spend on these processes can be redirected to support critical work on the ground to deliver results for children.  </p><p>But the GSSC is much more than that. We drive efficiency and improvement efforts for the entire organization. We also serve as a hub for various teams in UNICEF, bringing together policy and practice under one roof. As UNICEF continues to grow, so does the GSSC.  </p></div>
            </div>
      </div>
</div>

    <div class="comp-txt">
                            <div class="field paragraph field_component_text_content  odd-t text_long"><h3 class="text-align-center">Make a difference working with us </h3><p>UNICEF serves the most vulnerable children in over 190 countries, including emergency locations such as Ukraine, Yemen, Afghanistan, Myanmar, Haiti, etc.  The GSSC is constantly looking for new colleagues who are ready to contribute their skills in HR, finance, IT, and more to our mission. This way, you can play an important role in uplifting these children by taking care of the administrative needs of the colleagues serving in the field, allowing them to focus more time and energy on delivering results.  </p><p>No matter whether you are kickstarting your career or are a seasoned expert, we might have the perfect job for you. Joining the GSSC also opens the door to further learning and career growth, whether you want to </p><ul><li>sharpen your professional skills in a complex global organization,</li><li>meet and connect with international professionals working in the field and learn more about how UNICEF is building the future for children,</li><li>work in an office which is spearheading business innovation and promoting sustainable operations, or</li><li>take the first step towards an international career as part of the UNICEF family. </li></ul></div>

Search Close Search form Search Clear search input Search for result Hide filters Show filters Clear search input Search for result Max Clear search input Search for result Page Global Shared Services Centre Centralized HR, payroll, finance and IT services provided to UNICEF offices worldwide Home Global Shared Services Centre (GSSC) Transforming business Delivering results Work with the GSSC Consultant Portal UNICEF works in over 190 countries and territories to save children’s lives, to defend their rights, and to help them fulfil their potential, from early childhood through adolescence. Our organization’s activities focus on:  providing a safe and inclusive environment for children through adequate protection, reducing child mortality and child poverty by working to reach the most vulnerable children, supporting quality learning for every girl and boy, especially those left behind, reaching children and families with lifesaving aid and long-term assistance in emergencies, empower girls and women so that they can play a full role in society.  Embedded video follows Learn more about UNICEF’s mandate UNICEF staff in the field are doing all they can to reach the most vulnerable children across the world. But they also need support to stay fully focused on delivering the best possible results. That’s why we have a Global Shared Services Centre (GSSC) that takes care of these needs.   The GSSC supports more than 190 UNICEF offices and over 17 thousand staff worldwide with HR, payroll, finance and helpdesk services.   The centre is located in Budapest, Hungary – a country once a recipient of UNICEF’s support after World War II, now a host to several UN offices and an active contributor to fundraising for children. Explore vacancies with the UNICEF GSSC Learn about UNICEF Hungary’s charity work or donate UNICEF/UNI207962/Beguel What we do  We have over 400 dedicated staff members from all over the globe who provide services to UNICEF’s offices and staff worldwide, benchmarked against the highest industry standards.  Human resources – we help new colleagues onboard, parting colleagues offboard, and we take care of the HR needs of all staff members in-between Payroll – we coordinate salary disbursement globally Finance – we process invoices and provide a range of financial services to keep UNICEF programmes for children running Global helpdesk – we support staff in taking care of their work-related administrative tasks  Thanks to the GSSC, the reduced time - over 27,000 hours saved - that UNICEF offices spend on these processes can be redirected to support critical work on the ground to deliver results for children.   But the GSSC is much more than that. We drive efficiency and improvement efforts for the entire organization. We also serve as a hub for various teams in UNICEF, bringing together policy and practice under one roof. As UNICEF continues to grow, so does the GSSC.   Make a difference working with us  UNICEF serves the most vulnerable children in over 190 countries, including emergency locations such as Ukraine, Yemen, Afghanistan, Myanmar, Haiti, etc.  The GSSC is constantly looking for new colleagues who are ready to contribute their skills in HR, finance, IT, and more to our mission. This way, you can play an important role in uplifting these children by taking care of the administrative needs of the colleagues serving in the field, allowing them to focus more time and energy on delivering results.   No matter whether you are kickstarting your career or are a seasoned expert, we might have the perfect job for you. Joining the GSSC also opens the door to further learning and career growth, whether you want to  sharpen your professional skills in a complex global organization, meet and connect with international professionals working in the field and learn more about how UNICEF is building the future for children, work in an office which is spearheading business innovation and promoting sustainable operations, or take the first step towards an international career as part of the UNICEF family.  . Transforming business United Nations agencies are increasingly turning to shared services centres to improve efficiency and reduce costs by leveraging economies of scale in lower-cost locations. . Delivering results Reflecting on our 10 year journey, the GSSC has evolved from a transactional centre into a strategic partner for UNICEF, driving efficiency, delivering cost savings and reducing organizational risk across the globe. . Work with the GSSC Join the GSSC’s more than 400 staff, representing over 50 nationalities, who bring their diverse HR, payroll, finance, IT and operational expertise to every service.     <div class="comp-txt">
                            <div class="field paragraph field_component_text_content  odd-t text_long"><p>Protracted conflicts, climate shocks, economic instability and systemic discrimination exacerbate deprivations and inequalities, threatening decades of progress.</p><p><span class="secondary"><strong>This is a decisive moment</strong></span><br>The UNICEF Strategic Plan, 2026–2029, represents our commitment to accelerate the collaborative actions and investments needed to realize the rights of every child.</p><p><span class="secondary"><strong>We aim for transformative change</strong></span><br>Five new Impact Results tackle the most persistent barriers to children’s rights, by strengthening national systems that deliver for children:</p><ul><li>10 million child lives saved and at least 500 million children healthy, well-nourished and developmentally on-track.</li><li>350 million more children and young people learning and skilled.</li><li>100 million fewer children in multidimensional poverty.</li><li>350 million children protected from violence.</li><li>500 million children better protected from disasters and climate and environmental risks.</li></ul></div>

Search Close Search form Search Clear search input Search for result Hide filters Show filters Clear search input Search for result Max Clear search input Search for result Report UNICEF Strategic Plan 2026-2029 Advancing child rights, together UNICEF/UNI786806/Abdul Highlights Working together to secure children’s rights, now and in the future   UNICEF remains committed to advancing the full realization of children’s rights, leaving no child behind. In a world of complex, interconnected challenges and dwindling development funding, achieving this goal will take the concerted efforts and resources of a broad coalition of partners. The Strategic Plan, 2026–2029, is a call to action for governments, international organizations, civil society, the private sector and young people themselves to join us. Together, we can realize our shared vision: a world where every child survives and thrives, learns and develops skills for life, lives free from poverty and violence, and inherits a sustainable planet. Author(s) UNICEF Publication date July 2025 Languages Arabic, Chinese, English, French, Russian, Spanish Files available for download Arabic (pdf, 1 MB) Chinese (pdf, 937 KB) English (pdf, 826 KB) French (pdf, 920 KB) Russian (pdf, 797 KB) Spanish (pdf, 685 KB) Investment case for partners (pdf, 6 MB) Investment case (summary) (pdf, 2 MB) Download all files (zip, 13 MB) Children face unprecedented challenges Protracted conflicts, climate shocks, economic instability and systemic discrimination exacerbate deprivations and inequalities, threatening decades of progress. This is a decisive moment The UNICEF Strategic Plan, 2026–2029, represents our commitment to accelerate the collaborative actions and investments needed to realize the rights of every child. We aim for transformative change Five new Impact Results tackle the most persistent barriers to children’s rights, by strengthening national systems that deliver for children: 10 million child lives saved and at least 500 million children healthy, well-nourished and developmentally on-track. 350 million more children and young people learning and skilled. 100 million fewer children in multidimensional poverty. 350 million children protected from violence. 500 million children better protected from disasters and climate and environmental risks.
